# Dilith Dinesh — Product Portfolio

## About
Dilith Dinesh is a Customer Product Manager at Zuper,
a B2B SaaS company in field service management.
He is targeting Associate Product Manager (APM) and
AI-focused product roles at Series A/B product-led companies.

Positioning: Product operator at the boundary between
customer reality and product systems. Translates what
field teams actually experience into capabilities that scale.

Contact: dilithdinesh007@gmail.com
LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/in/dilithdinesh

## Work — Case Studies

### The Roofing Vertical
URL: https://dilithdinesh.com/work/golden-account-model
Tags: Zuper, Field Service, Systems Design
Summary: Built the roofing golden account — a fully
cloneable pre-configured Zuper account for roofing
contractors. Reduced onboarding from 12-16 weeks to
15 days. Used by 30+ contractor accounts. Every sales
demo runs on a clone of this account.
Skills demonstrated: vertical strategy, systems design,
ICP definition, workaround-to-requirement translation,
cross-functional influence without authority.

### The Stopgap That Knew Its Place
URL: https://dilithdinesh.com/work/booking-stopgap
Tags: Zuper, Field Service, Product Judgment
Summary: 9 of 15 roofing customers needed booking widgets.
Manual build took 1 day + 2 people each. Built a working
multi-tenant prototype in 6 hours using React, TypeScript,
Supabase. One call with the Principal PM got the native
feature back on the roadmap. Discovered and proactively
flagged 10DLC compliance requirement that was blocking
telephony approval for customers.
Skills demonstrated: build vs buy judgment, prototype
thinking, compliance awareness, stakeholder influence,
product requirements from real usage.

## Writing — Teardowns

### What B2B SaaS Can Learn From Rapido
URL: https://dilithdinesh.com/writing/rapido-teardown
Date: Jan 2026
Summary: Analysis of Rapido's growth from bike taxis to
habit loop. Four B2B SaaS lessons: start with undeniable
core value, expand after habit is built, optimize for
high-frequency low-friction use cases, build for actual
behavior not ideal behavior.

### How Spotify Turned Usage Data Into an Annual Identity Ritual
URL: https://dilithdinesh.com/writing/spotify-wrapped
Date: Dec 2025
Summary: Analysis of Spotify Wrapped's emotional architecture.
Core insight: data without interpretation is noise. Wrapped
succeeds by adding an interpretation layer that transforms
metrics into identity. Explores what B2B equivalent of a
shareable identity moment could look like.

## Projects — Build Logs

### Iris
URL: https://dilithdinesh.com/projects/iris
Stack: React 18, TypeScript, Supabase, Lovable
Summary: Private file and message transfer tool across
devices. Built because WhatsApp-as-file-transfer was
the only option. Multi-tenant architecture, 8-character
pairing codes, no user accounts required. Available on
Play Store. Went through full design system rebuild
(D-Chat to Iris) after neumorphic design failed in dark mode.

### Pulseboard
URL: https://dilithdinesh.com/projects/pulseboard
Stack: Lovable, Supabase, Claude, GPT-4
Summary: Personal work tracking and reflection app.
Built in one weekend. Logs daily activity, auto-categorizes
by work type and team, generates AI performance summaries.
Revealed that AI summaries handle volume well but not
weight — a gap identified for v2.
